title: Point-to-point routing across the road network (a dot travelling A to B)
summary: Pathfind a real connected route between two arbitrary points on the city-map's road graph, and render it as a travelling dot — instead of the current machinery, which only snaps a single point to its nearest road node.
description:
Ingram's own framing, verbatim, from a 'fun ideas for the wishlist' message: 'We could create a system which connects all road lines together so that we can actually draw a dot following the line of the road from A to B.'

What already exists, so this isn't starting from nothing: tools/city-map/citymap's RoadGraph (parse.py/world.py — node_xy, way_nodes, way_class, node_ways) is already a real connected planar graph built from OSM data, not disconnected line segments. ops/router.py already does curvature-constrained state-lattice A* pathfinding — but only for ONE job, construct.py's access-road routing, which pathfinds FROM a new building's fixed site TOWARD the nearest existing road. ops/trace.py explicitly does NOT do general pathfinding — its own module docstring says a hand-drawn trace's points already ARE the desired path, so there's 'nothing left to route around,' and reusing router.route() for that would be 'a different problem than what that router was built to answer.' That docstring is effectively pointing at the exact gap this idea fills: nothing today answers 'given point A and point B, both somewhere on the existing network, what connected sequence of roads gets between them?'

The likely shape: general point-to-point search (Dijkstra or A* with a real edge-length cost, reusing the existing node_xy/way_nodes adjacency rather than router.py's construct-specific lattice) that returns an ordered list of graph nodes/coordinates, plus a separate rendering concern — animating a marker along that polyline over time, for travel-time flavor between named locations (home, school, the Directorate facility, a Contact site) rather than just a static route overlay. Natural consumers: the map editor (tools/city-map/editor/) for GM-side route-planning, and/or the Foundry overworld Scene work (issue #107, module-stage-8-overworld-session-flow) if travel between sign-up locations ever wants a visual.

Recorded as a wishlist item, not a decision — the whether-to-build and the how are both open.

**Update, 2026-09-18 — Ingram answered the three open questions directly, promoting this to `accepted`.** (1) Render target is Foundry VTT's own main map Scene, not the local map editor or a standalone viewer — and per city-map-location-board.json's 2026-09-17 finding, a real 'Campaign Map' Scene already exists live on the server (12400x12400, four Tile documents), so there is a real Scene to animate tokens on today, not a hypothetical future one. (2) Disconnected-graph handling is settled as a universal fallback rather than an error case: when a route runs out of road or rail, the token 'walks' — leaves the network at the closest point reached and moves directly toward the next network point or the final destination, including straight across open water if that's what sits between two graph components. Ingram's own framing: 'Getting to the end destination is far more important than how we get there' — so a no-path result should downgrade visually (network-following to direct movement) and never hard-fail. (3) The real scope is bigger than one dot: the long-term goal is every travelling character's own unique token moving on its own leg of a journey, at the same time as others, using different transit logic per mode (walking, driving, rail, ferry), animated as one attractive, legible sequence whose whole point is to sell in-fiction travel distance and time as real. This is meant to be the visible other half of 'a system for allowing players to choose for themselves where they go' — i.e. the downtime/destination-choice work already designed in design/ux-doctrine.md (§3 downtime-as-scheduling-game, §7a the four-quarter day ring) and module/blank-inheritance/scripts/core/day-ring.mjs: a player picks a destination there, this is what shows them getting to it.

None of the multi-modal detail is designed yet — which graph a mode may use (rail graph only for a train, road graph for a car, any-or-off-graph for walking), how a token boards/alights a mode, and how in-fiction travel duration maps to watch-time are all still open, and are deliberately NOT being designed prematurely: per design/design-layers.md's own layering discipline, a single generic-speed mode with the walk-fallback above is the honest Layer 0 (removable, provably works on its own), and per-mode nuance is a later layer on top of a route/animate loop that already works. CLAUDE.md requires a check-in before writing actual Foundry module code rather than treating a design as a green light, so the pure routing logic (graph search + walk-fallback over tools/city-map's existing RoadGraph/rail graph, testable in isolation, no Foundry globals) is the part of Layer 0 that can start independently of that check-in once greenlit.

**Update, 2026-09-18, later the same day — the trigger vision, and Layer 0 built.** Ingram named the best-case trigger for this whole system: the scene-runner (module/blank-inheritance/scripts/foundry/scene-runner.mjs) ending a scene should be able to automatically start a process that cuts to the world map, animates every relevant character's token moving to its next destination at once, then cuts to the next scene — 'without anyone having to use a control.' This sits on top of, not instead of, the scene's own existing forced-choice closure step (core/scene-close.mjs's ending/cost dropdowns, design/ux-doctrine.md §10.3a's deliberate friction point) — see the new open question below on exactly how those two connect.

Layer 0 itself is now built: module/blank-inheritance/scripts/core/travel-route.mjs (+ test/tier1-travel-route.test.mjs, 9 tests, all passing) is a pure point-to-point router implementing exactly the 'ride the network as far as it usefully goes, walk the rest' rule — not shortest-path minimisation, which was tried first and rejected once the maths showed it would degenerate to never using the network at all (a straight line is always the shortest path between two points, so 'minimise total distance' can never prefer a detour through roads over one). Also implements the disconnected-graph fallback (ride to whichever reachable node ends up closest to the true destination, then walk). Zero Foundry dependency, confirmed by design/testing-strategy.md's own tier-0 architecture lint. Smoke-tested against the real exported road graph (tools/city-map, 178,950 nodes / 45,121 ways): a real cross-map route resolves correctly in ~1.9 seconds — a real, useful number for judging whether six simultaneous tokens needs a later optimisation pass, not yet a problem for a one-shot per-transition computation.

Not yet built, and deliberately out of this pass: the data-export step that gets a current graph snapshot OUT of tools/city-map's Python world and into the module (nothing today stages it — confirmed by reading tools/module-sync/stage-campaign-data.mjs directly); the conversion between the campaign map's pixel/grid space and this graph's own projected-metres space (two different coordinate systems, confirmed empirically, not yet bridged); and all of the Foundry-side adapter/animation work, which per CLAUDE.md needs its own check-in before it's written.

**Update, 2026-09-18, later still — the full choreography, and the trigger question resolved. Foundry-side work greenlit.** Ingram walked through the whole sequence end to end. The GM finishes a scene and hits a button. Scene A fades out over 10 seconds while the world map (the real 'Campaign Map' Scene) loads underneath. Every PC's token then moves at once from its current location to its destination via this system, with EACH PLAYER'S OWN VIEW acting as a camera following their own token — not one shared GM view. The camera starts zoomed out on the whole map, zooms in during the movement, then zooms back out at the destination to re-establish context. Then a fade to black, then a 10-second fade into Scene B. Named goal, verbatim: 'like a really attractive fast travel game animation.' Multi-speed modes (train/bike/walk) stay future work, unchanged from what's already recorded above.

This resolves the trigger question (moved to resolvedSubQuestions below) — with one flagged assumption: 'hitting a button' is read here as the EXISTING manual scene-close confirm (core/scene-close.mjs's forced ending/cost dropdowns), since Ingram described a single action without mentioning those dropdowns one way or the other. Law 15's deliberate friction (design/ux-doctrine.md §10.3a) is assumed to stay exactly as designed, with this whole sequence firing AFTER that choice is made, not instead of it. Flag and correct if that reading is wrong.

Also split out: the 10-second fade is wanted between ALL scene activations as a general rule, independent of travel entirely (it should fire even when nothing is moving) — recorded separately as ideas/entries/scene-transition-fades.json rather than folded in here, since it applies even without this system.

**Given the size of the full choreography, the honest Layer 1 (greenlit 2026-09-18, starting now) is deliberately smaller than all of it:** get one token actually animating along a `planRoute()`-computed path on the real Campaign Map Scene — no per-player camera-follow, no zoom staging, no fades yet. Prove the mechanism itself first, per design/design-layers.md's own rule that a layer earns the next one by working on its own. Camera-follow, zoom choreography and fades are real, named, and NOT forgotten — they are Layer 2, tracked here, not built yet.

**Update, 2026-09-18, the data export ran for real.** tools/gazetteer/export_travel_graph.py now exists: it reuses tools/city-map/render.py's own world-resolution path (so this never drifts from what a real render shows), merges road_graph + rail_graph, and converts every node through the map's own georeferencing (tools/gazetteer/core/georef.py's `source_to_image_px` — the existing, tested, rotation-aware transform; no second copy needed in JS). Real numbers from the actual campaign city: 188,453 nodes / 46,884 ways merged, clipping to the visible 12km map content area brings that down to 64,307 nodes / 19,514 ways, written to data/map/travel-graph.json (3.73 MB). Loaded straight into planRoute() with zero further conversion: a real cross-map route over the real network resolves in ~435ms (down from ~1.9s unclipped — clipping to content bounds was worth doing). Coordinate-space bridging is therefore DONE for Layer 1, not just scoped.

**Update, 2026-09-18 — Layer 1 live-verified end to end in the local Foundry test world.** module/blank-inheritance/scripts/core/travel-animation.mjs (+ test/tier1-travel-animation.test.mjs, 5 tests) adds the last pure piece: `flattenRoute` (de-duplicates a planRoute() segment list into one point list) and `hopDurations` (splits a total travel time across hops proportionally to each hop's share of the route's real length, so a long straight stretch is watched proportionally longer than a short one) — deliberately NOT a custom animation loop, since Foundry's own `TokenDocument#update(data, {animation:{duration}})` already tweens a single hop smoothly; chaining real hops through it reuses Foundry's own animation rather than reimplementing one.

Proven live: created a token on the local test world's own map Scene ('The City' — see the naming/versioning note below), fed it a real planRoute() result between two real points ~325m apart (a genuine 35-hop road-following path, run through flattenRoute + hopDurations at an 8-second total travel time), and watched it animate hop by hop to a pixel-exact stop at the destination, sitting correctly on a real street per the map art. This confirms the FULL chain end to end: Python export -> real graph -> JS Dijkstra -> georeferenced scene coordinates -> real Foundry Token animation.

**A real naming/versioning discrepancy found, not resolved:** the local test world has NO Scene called 'Campaign Map'. Its own map Scene is named 'The City' (module/blank-inheritance/assets/scenes/campaign-map.webp, 6200x6200 -- exactly half the 12400 master, single background image, Scene padding 0, zero Tiles) -- different in name, size, AND construction (one image vs. four Tiles) from what city-map-location-board.json recorded checking on the REMOTE production server on 2026-09-17. Both may be correct for their own copy (local dev vs. live production may simply be out of sync, which module-sync's existence already implies is normal), but this wasn't reconciled -- flagging rather than guessing which is authoritative. The coordinate bridge itself does not care: `scale = scene.width / campaign-map.json's image.width` is computed from whichever Scene is actually live, so it is correct either way without a code change.

**Still not wired up, and deliberately not attempted in this pass:** this proof fed the adapter a route computed and pre-scaled in Node, pasted in -- there is still no code path that (a) loads data/map/travel-graph.json INTO the running module (nothing stages it into module/blank-inheritance/ the way data/campaign/ is staged, and tools/module-sync/stage-campaign-data.mjs was mid-edit by other uncommitted work this session, deliberately left untouched rather than risk colliding with it), or (b) decides which two points to route between from real game state (a Token's current position, a chosen destination) rather than two hand-picked test coordinates. Those are Layer 1's real remaining gap, not Layer 2's camera/zoom/fade choreography.

**Update, 2026-09-18, corrected: Ingram checks the REMOTE server, not local, and the remote map is the right one.** 'Anything you've built for the local server needs to also be on the remote server. I only check the remote server' — then, on the naming/versioning question above: 'The remote server has the right version of the map... Full resolution and it's across four tiles... We need the full resolution for it to look good.' So 'The City' (local, 6200x6200, one downscaled background) was the lesser copy, not the current one — the real target is the remote's actual 'Campaign Map' Scene.

Read that real Scene directly rather than re-guessing: copied its LevelDB store down from the server (tools/pack-extractor, the same reader already built for sf2e's compendium packs — generic to any Foundry classic-level store, not just packs) and parsed it locally. Confirmed: 12400x12400, 4 real Tile documents, each a genuine unscaled 6200x6200 PNG (checked against the file's own PNG header on the server, not assumed) at canvas (6300,6300)/(12500,6300)/(6300,12500)/(12500,12500). **That exposed a real bug in the Layer 1 math**: the original scale-only model (verified against 'The City', where the offset happens to be zero) has no origin term at all, and the real Scene needs one — (6300,6300), which does NOT equal `12400 * 0.25` (the Scene's own `padding` field), so guessing from `padding` would ALSO have been wrong. Fixed in travel-animation.mjs: `sceneCalibration(tiles, sceneWidth, manifestImageWidth)` derives origin + scale from the Scene's own tile bounding box when tiles exist, falling back to the original scale-only/zero-origin case for a plain background scene. Regression-tested against the real pulled numbers (test/tier1-travel-animation.test.mjs), not a synthetic fixture.

Both travel-route.mjs and the corrected travel-animation.mjs are now verified-pushed to the remote server itself (tools/module-sync/sync-module.mjs, checksum-confirmed both sides) — scoped to just those two files via `--local-dir` pointed at a temp staging copy, specifically to avoid also pushing other sessions' unrelated uncommitted module changes live as a side effect. The corrected coordinate math has NOT yet been live-animated against the real production Campaign Map Scene itself (only unit-tested against its real, pulled numbers) — creating a test token on the actual campaign world felt like it warranted asking first, unlike the local throwaway world.

**Update, 2026-09-18, later still — Layer 2's minimal slice built, as part of bringing everything built this fortnight into one working system.** Ingram's own answer, asked directly: "Finish it properly now — I want all movement of characters between scenes to involve cutting to the world map between... scene -> map -> scene -> map -> scene -> map etc etc." This is the FULL choreography's trigger and the campaign-map crossing itself, not the per-player camera work: `data/map/travel-graph.json` and `data/map/campaign-map.json` are now staged into the module (`tools/module-sync/stage-campaign-data.mjs`'s new `SYNCED_MAP_FILES` — two named files, not the whole 115MB+ `data/map/` directory that reasoning has always excluded). The two real points to route between are decided from real game state, closing the gap the previous update named: `foundry/scene-build.mjs` already stamps every real Scene with its own `locationRef` flag, so a new pure gate (`core/travel-trigger.mjs#needsTravel`) checks whether the scene being left and the scene being cut to actually name different locations, and `foundry/scene-runner.mjs`'s own "Cut To" action reads both flags directly rather than needing any new UI. When they differ, `foundry/travel.mjs#runTravelSequence` runs the ritual: cue the campaign-map hub scene with a real 10-second fade (Foundry's own native `TextureTransitionFilter`, confirmed to already support exactly this via `director-panel.mjs`'s existing `cueScene(..., {transitionType, transitionDuration})` — no custom fade implementation needed, answering this file's own open question about reusing Foundry's native transition), animate the party's marker hop by hop along the real routed path (the already-built travel-route.mjs/travel-animation.mjs chain, finally with a real caller), then cut on to the destination with the same fade. Never blocks arrival: a missing hub scene, an unmapped location, or a graph that fails to load all fall back to a plain cut. **What this is NOT**: per-player camera-follow and the zoom-out/in/out choreography are still entirely unbuilt — today's crossing is one shared view for the whole table, not each player's own camera following their own token. The marker is also a single shared token standing in for the whole party, not one token per PC — matching what Session 0/1 actually needs (nobody has a placed token of their own yet at the point this fires) rather than the full named vision. Automated coverage: `test/tier1-travel-trigger.test.mjs`, `test/tier3-travel-contract.test.mjs`, and new cases in `test/module-sync/stage-campaign-data.test.mjs`. **Not yet live-verified against a real running Foundry world** — see this entry's own resolution field.
sourceContext: Ingram, in a message offering 'some fun ideas to record to the wish list of Github issue tracker' (alongside the afterschool-club idea folded into school-schedule-system.json).
openSubQuestions: Point-to-point search over the existing RoadGraph adjacency directly, or does ops/router.py's existing A* generalize to this with its lattice/curvature constraints relaxed? (Leaning toward plain Dijkstra/A* over node_xy/way_nodes directly — router.py's curvature/grade constraints solve a different problem, buildable new roads, that a token merely following existing roads doesn't have.)

Which graph may a given transit mode use, and how does a token board/alight one — rail graph only for a train, road graph only for a car, any-graph-or-off-graph for walking? Needs the mode roster (walk/drive/rail/ferry) actually named first.

How should in-fiction travel duration map to on-screen animation time — does a cross-city train ride watch longer than a short walk, or is everything normalized to a similar watch-length regardless of in-fiction distance?

How does this wire into the destination-choice system (day-ring.mjs / downtime scheduling)? Does picking a destination there trigger the animation automatically, and what happens when several PCs choose different destinations in the same slice — do all their tokens animate at once?
resolvedSubQuestions: Consumer, resolved 2026-09-18: Foundry VTT's own main map Scene — specifically the real, live 'Campaign Map' Scene (12400x12400, four Tiles) that city-map-location-board.json confirmed exists on the server as of 2026-09-17. Not the local map editor, not a standalone viewer.

Static render vs. animation, resolved 2026-09-18: real animated movement, and not just one dot — the goal is every travelling character's own unique token moving at once, because the animation's whole purpose is to sell in-fiction travel distance and time as real.

Disconnected-graph behaviour, resolved 2026-09-18: a universal 'walk' fallback, never a hard failure. When the route runs out of road/rail, the token moves directly toward the next network point or the final destination, including straight across open water if that's the gap. Ingram's framing: 'Getting to the end destination is far more important than how we get there.'

Trigger vs. the existing manual scene-close flow, resolved 2026-09-18 (with one flagged assumption — see the update in the description): the sequence fires when the GM 'hits a button' to advance, read as the existing scene-close confirm rather than a new separate control. Full choreography: Scene A fades out 10s -> world map loads -> every PC token moves at once, each player's own view following their own token as camera, zoomed out -> in -> out -> a fade to black -> a 10s fade into Scene B. Law 15's forced ending/cost choice is untouched by this, firing before it as it does today.
relatedRefs: GitHub issue #107 (Build the overworld Scene from a real tools/city-map render) — the real 'Campaign Map' Scene now confirms this consumer
resolution: 2026-09-18: Ingram made a basic (single-mode, walk-fallback) working version of this a tracked requirement for Session 0/1 readiness — added as a new unchecked item under GitHub issue #140's Technical/UI checklist. Layer 0 and Layer 1 (the pure router and the coordinate bridge) were built and live-verified the same day. Later the same day, greenlit again ('finish it properly now') as part of unifying everything built over the prior two weeks into one working system: Layer 2's minimal slice (the scene-runner trigger, the campaign-map crossing itself, and the fade either side) is now built too — see the description's own final dated update. GitHub issue #140's checklist item stays unchecked pending a live run against a real Foundry world; per-player camera-follow and zoom choreography remain unbuilt and out of scope for Session 0/1.
